channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Kazakhstan Faces Donor Shortage in Kidney Transplants, Fueling Illegal Market
item.description: Kazakhstan's advanced kidney transplant program is hampered by a severe donor shortage, leading to illegal transplants and a black market. While the state covers transplant costs, only 6-7 out of 10 dialysis patients are eligible due to post-surgery medication and health requirements. Donor scarcity and patient ineligibility remain critical issues.

item.title: Kazakhstan's 'Umai' Women's Mortgage Program Reaches 20 Billion Tenge Limit in Hours
item.description: The 'Umai' mortgage program, specifically designed for women in Kazakhstan, reached its 20 billion tenge funding limit within hours of its launch. This rapid uptake indicates strong demand for specialized housing finance solutions among women in the country.

item.title: Tajikistan and China May Establish Joint Pharmaceutical Production Enterprises
item.description: Tajikistan and Chinese investors are exploring the creation of joint ventures for pharmaceutical production. Discussions focused on investment cooperation, project implementation, and attracting foreign investment in Tajikistan's pharmaceutical sector, including adopting advanced Chinese technologies.

item.title: Blogger Criticizes High Toll for Bishkek's Eastern Bypass Road
item.description: Activist Dmitry Luzhansky has questioned the proposed 500 som toll for Bishkek's new Eastern bypass road, deeming it excessively high. He suggests a maximum of 350 som, comparing the cost per kilometer to other toll roads and taxi fares during peak hours.

item.title: New International Airport Under Construction in Jalal-Abad, Kyrgyzstan
item.description: A new international airport is being built in the Suzak district of Kyrgyzstan's Jalal-Abad region. The project includes a 3800-meter runway and a modern terminal designed for 350 passengers per hour. Construction began in May 2025, with completion expected in Q3 2027.

item.title: Digital Economy: A Prerequisite for Sustainable Development in Kazakhstan
item.description: Kazakhstan's President's Address outlines a new era of development, emphasizing the creation of a modern infrastructure and a strong economy for future generations. The digital economy, integrating technologies like AI, is presented as crucial for modernizing traditional sectors and fostering sustainable growth.

item.title: Kazakhstan's President Tokayev Calls for Fundamental Review of Social Policy
item.description: President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev of Kazakhstan has criticized the current social security system, citing widespread corruption and institutional negligence. He emphasized that social support should genuinely aid those in need, rather than masking governmental shortcomings or fostering dependency. The President called for a strategic reorientation of social policy to focus on long-term goals over temporary fixes.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Proposes 50-Meter Distance Rule for Trucks on Highways, New Fines
item.description: Kyrgyzstan is considering a new law requiring trucks over 3.5 tons to maintain a minimum 50-meter distance on intercity roads when traveling over 50 km/h. The proposed legislation aims to reduce accidents caused by insufficient spacing between heavy vehicles. The bill suggests fines for violations, though there's an inconsistency regarding the penalty amounts.

item.title: Kazakhstan Discusses President Tokayev's Strategic Address on National Development
item.description: An analytical center in Astana hosted a roundtable to discuss President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev's address to the nation. Participants, including public figures and experts, focused on priority development areas, economic and social challenges, and key tasks for Kazakhstan's new historical phase. The discussion emphasized translating reforms into tangible results for citizens.

item.title: Belarusian President Predicts End to Ukraine War in Coming Months
item.description: Belarusian President Alexander Lukashenko stated that the war in Ukraine will conclude within the next few months, citing a lack of resources and widespread fatigue. He believes Europe is beginning to understand the origins of the escalation. Minsk is open to hosting negotiations without intermediaries.

item.title: Kazakhstan Approves National Action Plan to Implement President's Address
item.description: The draft National Action Plan for implementing President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev's address has been approved by the government. The plan outlines 96 measures across 12 socio-economic development areas, including industrial and agricultural support, digital solutions, and tax system improvements.

item.title: Kazakhstan Pursues Technological Independence Through AI and Digital Economy
item.description: Kazakhstan is enhancing its digital technological potential, aiming to become a leader in the field. A recent project with NVIDIA has garnered international attention. The country seeks to transform energy resources into high-value intellectual products, strengthening technological sovereignty and diversifying its economy away from raw material dependence.

item.title: Cheaper Generic Version of HIV Prevention Drug Approved
item.description: The US FDA has approved a generic version of the lenacapavir drug for HIV prevention. This makes the medication more accessible and affordable for residents in 120 countries. The new option allows for a cheaper PrEP alternative for individuals at high risk of HIV infection, administered via injection every three months.

item.title: Former MP and IT Head Appointed as Deputy Defense Ministers in Kazakhstan
item.description: Former Parliament member Tatyana Savelieva and ex-head of "National Information Technologies" Daulet Bekmanov have been appointed as Deputy Ministers of Defense in Kazakhstan. Their roles, which do not require military service, focus on economics and finance for Savelieva, and digitalization for Bekmanov. Both are civilian personnel within the Ministry of Defense.

item.title: Uzbekistan's WTO Accession May Be Delayed Beyond 2026, Negotiations Expected to Be Difficult
item.description: Uzbekistan's accession to the World Trade Organization (WTO), initially anticipated for 2026, may be postponed to 2027. Reports indicate that negotiations are proving to be challenging. The country has been working towards WTO membership, with updated expectations now pointing to a later date for finalization.

item.title: Kazakhstan Police Arrest 21 in Connection with Illegal Sale of Potent Medications
item.description: Kazakhstan police have detained 21 individuals, including pharmaceutical company owners and employees, suspected of illegally selling potent medications. Over 50,000 vials of 'Tropikamed' were seized, along with weapons, vehicles, and large sums of money. The operation targeted illegal distribution channels in Akmola and Karaganda regions.

item.title: Kazakh Wrestlers Nursultan Sadik and Sabina Torey Banned for Two Years Due to Doping Violations
item.description: Kazakh wrestlers Nursultan Sadik and Sabina Torey have been suspended from competitions for two years for violating anti-doping rules. Sadik tested positive for clomiphene and will be banned until January 2028. Torey tested positive for sibutramine and will be banned until August 2028. Both athletes have achieved notable results in national and international competitions.

item.title: Kazakhstan Plans to Increase Maternity and Childcare Benefits Following Minimum Wage Hike
item.description: Kazakhstan is set to increase maternity and childcare benefits starting next year due to a planned rise in the minimum wage from 85,000 to 110,000 tenge. This adjustment will affect the calculation limits for social insurance payments. The maximum monthly childcare payment could rise to 308,000 tenge, an increase of 70,000 tenge.

item.title: Tajikistan Aims to Reduce Greenhouse Gas Emissions by 15% by 2035, Potentially 40% with Support
item.description: Tajikistan intends to reduce greenhouse gas emissions by 15% by 2035 compared to 1990 levels, with the potential to reach 40% with international financial and technological support. This was announced at a round table in Dushanbe on November 3, 2026, discussing the country's climate priorities and its Nationally Determined Contribution (NDC) 3.0.

item.title: Experts Predict Fuel Prices to Rise in Kazakhstan This November
item.description: Experts forecast a potential increase in gasoline and diesel fuel prices in Kazakhstan this November, though the rise is expected to be gradual and varied across regions. While wholesale prices for AI-92 gasoline and diesel may increase by up to 10,000 tenge per ton, factors like existing reserves and competition may prevent a sharp surge at the pump.

item.title: Tashkent Metro Considers Introducing Women-Only Carriages to Reduce Harassment
item.description: The Tashkent Metro is considering the introduction of special women-only carriages to reduce instances of harassment. While currently lacking the technical capacity, the metro administration noted that this could be incorporated into future line construction and carriage purchases. Similar practices exist in countries like India, Egypt, and Iran.

item.title: Ata Jurt Activists Face Restrictions After Sentencing for Discrimination Advocacy
item.description: Nazygul Maksutkhan, a lawyer for the Ata Jurt organization, which documented discrimination against Kazakhs and Uyghurs in China, has been sentenced to four years and eight months of restricted freedom. Her brother received a five-year prison sentence. The charges stem from an unauthorized protest.

item.title: Spanish Transport Minister Resigns Following Deadly Train Collision
item.description: Spain's Transport Minister, Óscar Puente, has resigned following a high-speed train collision near Urdan that killed at least 69 people and injured dozens. Puente cited "political pride and conscience" for his decision, acknowledging a loss of public trust in the high-speed rail system.

item.title: Greenland Parliament Ratifies Security Agreement with the United States
item.description: Greenland's parliament has ratified a security agreement with the United States, signed earlier this year. The deal expands the U.S. military's role on the Arctic island, including new bases and a missile defense system, while reaffirming Danish sovereignty and Greenland's self-determination.

item.title: Earthquake in Kyrgyzstan Felt in Fergana Valley with Magnitude 2-3
item.description: An earthquake with a magnitude of 2-3 was felt in the Fergana Valley regions on November 4th at 02:34 local time. The epicenter was located in the Osh region of Kyrgyzstan, with a magnitude of 5.2 and a depth of 10 km. The tremors were felt in Andijan, Fergana, and Namangan regions.

item.title: China-Kyrgyzstan-Uzbekistan Railway Construction Advances with Tunnel and Bridge Work
item.description: Construction on the China-Kyrgyzstan-Uzbekistan railway is progressing, with significant work completed on tunnels and bridges in Kyrgyzstan. Kyrgyz Railways reports that approximately 22% of the total construction is expected to be finished by the end of 2026. The project aims for a 2031 operational launch, potentially earlier.

item.title: Afghan-Pakistan Conflict Hinders Central-South Asian Trade, Kazakhstan Revises Targets
item.description: The ongoing conflict between Afghanistan and Pakistan is significantly hindering trade between Central and South Asia. Kazakhstan has revised its annual bilateral trade turnover target with Pakistan downwards to approximately $645 million, a decrease from earlier optimistic projections. Uzbekistan also faces challenges in meeting its trade goals.

item.title: Uzbekistan Focuses on Professional Training for Labor Migrants
item.description: Uzbekistan is enhancing its state policy in employment by focusing on professional training for labor migrants. The goal is to prepare citizens not just as a workforce, but as professionals with modern skills and foreign language proficiency. This initiative aims to expand opportunities for young people seeking employment abroad.

item.title: Uzbekistan's Mining Industry Reviews Performance and Sets Future Goals
item.description: Uzbekistan's Ministry of Mining Industry and Geology held a meeting to analyze the sector's performance from January to September. Key priorities include modernizing processes, expanding geological exploration, optimizing resource use, and enhancing enterprise efficiency. The ministry aims to strengthen control over digitalization and ensure the implementation of set tasks.

item.title: Asian Cup Football Tournament Postponed to Late 2027 Due to Regional Instability
item.description: The Asian Football Confederation (AFC) has postponed the 2027 Asian Cup, originally scheduled for January 2027, to December 2027-January 2028. The decision cites "exceptional circumstances" and "logistical complexities" arising from Middle East conflict. This impacts preparations for qualified teams including Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan, and Uzbekistan.

item.title: Uzbekistan Modernizes Bukhara Oil Refinery to Boost High-Quality Fuel Production
item.description: President Shavkat Mirziyoyev visited the Bukhara Oil Refinery to review a modernization project aimed at increasing crude processing capacity by 2.5 million tons annually. The $328 million project will enhance production of Euro-5 compliant gasoline (AI-92 and AI-95) by installing hydrotreating and naphtha isomerization units.

item.title: SCO Plus Security Dialogue on Digital Transformation to Convene in Samarkand
item.description: The first SCO Plus expert dialogue on security, focusing on countering terrorism and extremism in the digital age, will be held in Samarkand from November 5-6, 2026. The initiative, proposed by Uzbekistan's President Shavkat Mirziyoyev, will be chaired by the head of Uzbekistan's State Security Service. The event will gather representatives from SCO member states, observers, dialogue partners, and international organizations to discuss the impact of new technologies on security challenges.

item.title: Uzbekistan's WTO Accession: Progress and Future Tasks Discussed in Tashkent
item.description: A press conference in Tashkent reviewed Uzbekistan's progress in joining the World Trade Organization. Discussions covered economic reforms, results of negotiation rounds, and upcoming priorities. Over 400 questions from member states were addressed, and significant progress was made in bilateral negotiations on market access for goods and services. WTO accession aims to expand foreign trade and improve the investment climate.

item.title: US Assistant Secretary of State Visits Turkmenistan to Boost Ties
item.description: US Assistant Secretary of State for South and Central Asia, Paul Kapur, has arrived in Turkmenistan for a visit aimed at strengthening bilateral relations. The visit focuses on expanding business ties, energy cooperation, and regional connectivity, following Secretary of State Marco Rubio's recent trip to Central Asia.

item.title: Namangan Region and Italy Sign Mutually Beneficial Agreements
item.description: A delegation led by the governor of Namangan region, Shavkat Abdurazzakov, visited Italy and held meetings with regional president Michele de Pascale. Discussions focused on cooperation in industry, textiles, and manufacturing, with an emphasis on high value-added products. Agreements were reached to develop interregional ties and attract Italian investment to Namangan.

item.title: Turkmenistan Security Council Reviews Ten-Month Performance, Discusses Security Enhancements
item.description: Turkmenistan's President Serdar Berdimuhamedow chaired a Security Council meeting reviewing the performance of military and law enforcement agencies over the past ten months. Discussions focused on ensuring national security and stability, strengthening the material and technical base of these agencies, and further improving their operations. The meeting also covered the progress of the conscription season and professional development of military personnel.

item.title: President of Turkmenistan Receives President of the Federal Council of Austria
item.description: President Serdar Berdimuhamedow met with Kristina Schwanberg, President of the Federal Council of the Republic of Austria. Schwanberg conveyed greetings from Austrian President Alexander Van der Bellen. Both leaders emphasized the strong, mutually respectful relations between Turkmenistan and Austria, including parliamentary cooperation.

item.title: Turkmen President meets with head of Toyo Engineering Corporation
item.description: President Serdar Berdimuhamedow received Eiji Hosoi, president of Japan's Toyo Engineering Corporation. Hosoi expressed gratitude for the opportunity and highlighted Japan's emphasis on bilateral relations. The meeting focused on cooperation in Turkmenistan's construction, industrial, chemical, and energy sectors, building on long-standing projects in the gas and chemical industries.

item.title: Kazakh Seafarer Among Crew Released from India-Arrested Tanker
item.description: A second group of seven sailors, including a citizen of Kazakhstan, has been removed from the tanker Unity, arrested in India. The Kazakh Foreign Ministry confirmed preparations for his return. The first group of seven sailors has already returned home. Nine crew members remain awaiting a replacement team.

item.title: Linguistic Discrimination in Badakhshan: Pashto Imposed Over Local Persian and Uzbek Languages
item.description: The imposition of Pashto in public messages and banners in Badakhshan raises concerns about linguistic justice and equality. While respecting all languages, the article argues that neglecting the dominant Persian and spoken Uzbek languages in favor of Pashto disregards the identity and dignity of local residents. The author questions why public communications are not in languages understood by the local population.
